subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Why Engineers Need Ethics: Lessons From Disaster
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Why Engineers Need Ethics: Lessons From Disaster.

hook.text: Engineers hold public safety in their hands. When they cut corners or stay silent, people die.

buildup.text: Professional engineering codes require prioritizing public safety above client wishes, employer demands, and personal gain.

discovery.text: Whistleblower protections exist because speaking up can end careers. Roger Boisjoly warned about Challenger and was sidelined.

twist.text: The Ford Pinto cost-benefit analysis valued human life at $200,000. Ford decided recalls were more expensive than lawsuits.

climax.text: Modern engineering ethics education uses case studies from real disasters. Every failure teaches a principle.

punchline.text: Engineering is not just math and materials. It's responsibility.

quiz.question: What happened to Roger Boisjoly after he warned about the Challenger O-rings?
options: He was promoted for his courage and given a leadership role
He was sidelined by his employer despite being proven correct
He resigned before the launch and started his own engineering firm
